findings.label: The licences differ and one is a hazard: OpenBot is MIT, OpenMausBot, rakazo, turnstone and buzz are Apache 2.0, OpenGhost and hermes-muse are MIT, and openhuman is GPL-3.0, so nothing from it can be lifted into a permissively licensed product.

rakazo's packages/core/src/integrations/vault.ts is 174 lines of TypeScript under Apache 2.0 and is the closest drop-in for the secret store's policy layer, carrying siteHost, secretAnswerRefusal and the fixed-refusal vocabulary.
rakazo's packages/core/src/node/secrets-guard.ts is 188 lines and is a placeholder guard rather than a store: it refuses dev placeholders at startup instead of holding a value.
rakazo's packages/core/src/messages/secret-matcher.ts is 199 lines and is the leak-detection equivalent of skilled bots' findSecretLiteral.
OpenBot's shared/computer-token.ts is 70 lines of MIT TypeScript and is a self-contained HMAC derivation with a versioned label, liftable as-is if per-bot tokens are ever needed.
OpenBot's shared/computer-start.ts is 13 lines, so the container spec is configuration rather than code and there is nothing to lift.
turnstone's keyring is Python using Fernet, so its rule is liftable and its code is not.
The reuse list is three TypeScript files from rakazo and one from OpenBot, all permissive, totalling about 630 lines of reference rather than code to copy wholesale.

ruledOut.reason: GPL-3.0 is copyleft and a permissively licensed product cannot absorb it
it is Python and the per-user path is dark by default, so the rule is worth more than the code
it is an OpenAPI description of a server this product does not have, so the shape transfers and the code does not
